name: Ask what is causing symptoms
definition: The participant describes their own or someone else's symptoms or health change and asks what could be causing it or what it means. This includes asking why they feel a certain way emotionally (for example, why am I anxious). The help wanted is an explanation or likely diagnosis for a specific personal situation.
signs:
- "What could be causing this?" or "what could be the problem"
- "What did I catch?" or "what kind of injury does this sound like"
- "Could it be X or Y?" offering candidate causes
- "Is that typical" or "Does that make sense?" about a described personal symptom
- "How do I know if I have X"
how_it_differs: This code needs a personal case described in the message and a question about what is behind it. If the question is about a condition, medicine or procedure in general, use General health facts. A message can carry both (e.g. "Could it be gastritis? Tell me what causes gastritis"); code both.
example_1: "Sometimes I wake up feeling like I haven't rested at all. What could be causing this?" (63e55f08)
example_2: "nose is congested. What did I catch?" (664639e0)
example_3: "what kind of knee injury does this sound like" (69fff128)
merge_note: All three passes had this code with near-identical chat sets. Passes 2 and 3 included 'is that typical / does that make sense' questions about a personal symptom here, whereas pass 1 split these off as 'Check if normal or safe' (dropped); the merged definition follows the majority.

name: General health facts
definition: The participant asks for general information about a condition, symptom, test, procedure, medicine or health measure, not tied to explaining their own case. This includes definitions, symptom lists, causes, norms, statistics and likely outcomes.
signs:
- "What is X?" or "symptoms of X"
- "Can X ...?" or "Does X ...?" general yes-or-no fact questions
- "List every ..." or "Percentage of people ..."
- "What if X isn't treated" or "what causes X and how long can it last"
- "What will they do" at a test or appointment
how_it_differs: General health facts asks how health works in general; Ask what is causing symptoms asks to explain a specific personal case. Decide by whether the question is about the person's own described symptoms (code R1) or about a named condition or topic in general (code R2); code both if both are asked.
example_2: "please list every disease where fistula-in-anu is a symptom" (6658d49a)
example_3: "What is the normal weight for a male who is 28 and five feet nine inches tall?" (6952e59d)
merge_note: Same name and largely the same chats in all passes. Passes 2 and 3 included 'what will they do' at an appointment (6a106089) here; pass 1 put it under medical care. The merged definition follows the majority and includes what to expect from a test or procedure.

name: Ask what to do or whether it is safe
definition: The participant asks what they (or the person they care for) can do, take, change or safely do to relieve, treat or manage a current health problem or recovery. This includes whether an everyday activity (drinking, exercise, food) is safe right now, and how to cope with stress or emotional strain. The help wanted is practical self-care or treatment advice.
signs:
- "What should I take?"
- "What can I do to help/alleviate..."
- "How to heal X"
- "what do I do?" after describing a problem
- "Would switching ... help" about adjusting a current treatment
- "Should I/you be [doing an everyday activity]" or "is it safe to ..." during a current problem or recovery
- Asks how to cope with stress or emotional strain
- Asks for a supplement or product to treat named conditions
how_it_differs: This code asks for self-care, medicine, habit or safety steps for a current problem. If the only choice being weighed is whether or when to see, call or use a professional or procedure, use Whether to seek medical care. If the request is goal-driven (fitness, nutrition) rather than problem-driven, use Personal plan or recommendations. A supplement or product asked for to treat NAMED conditions is this code; add Personal plan or recommendations only if a wellness or fitness goal is also stated.
example_1: "I have a headache, what should I take?" (69fd05bd)
example_2: "what can i do to alleviate knee pain and get back to normal?" (69fb8bf7)
example_3: "How to heal neuropathy pain in leg" (66d9e5be)
pass2_code: Asking what to do for relief
merge_note: All three passes agreed on this code. Pass 3 also placed 69d51123 (drinking after surgery) here, while passes 1 and 2 treated it as a safety/decision question; the boundary with R5 is noted. 6a0206ae (wanting to talk about stress and what to do) was placed here by all passes.

name: Information shared without a question
definition: The participant states a symptom, health detail or test result with no explicit question or request, leaving the AI to infer what help is wanted (usually an assessment). This includes bare symptom phrases and pasted reports or lab values.
signs:
- A short symptom phrase with no question, e.g. "CHEST PAIN WHEN RUNNING"
- A statement about someone's symptom or a noticed change, with no request
- Age plus a test value, e.g. "72 yo woman with 6.0 a1c"
- A pasted lab or imaging report with no request
how_it_differs: Use this code only when no question or request is stated. If the message explicitly asks what is causing it, what it is, or what to do, code that request instead.
pass2_code: Stating a symptom or result only
merge_note: All three passes had this code. Passes 2 and 3 included bare test results (66ec5904, 6a638cf5) here, while pass 1 put them in a separate 'Interpret results or numbers' code (dropped). The merged code follows the majority and covers both symptoms and results.

name: Whether to seek medical care
definition: The participant asks whether they should see a doctor or specialist, have a procedure, or contact their care team, or when to do so. This includes asking whether a recommended procedure is necessary for them. The help wanted is a judgement on a specific decision about using professional care.
signs:
- "Should I see a medical specialist ... or try to wait it out?"
- "Would an endocrinologist benefit me"
- "Is it a must?" about a procedure
- Checking when they can or should call the care team
closest_other: Ask what to do or whether it is safe
how_it_differs: This code is about a named decision to use (or not use) professional care, or its timing. If the person asks for self-care, medicine or habit steps, use Ask what to do or whether it is safe. A general question about what happens at an appointment is General health facts.
example_1: "Should I see a medical specialist about this or try to wait it out?" (697cba85)
example_2: "Would an endocrinologist benefit me from learning why my hormones are our of whack?" (6abae4ea)
example_3: "Percentage of people need to get 2nd eye's cataract surgery after doing the first one. Is it a must?" (69f441ce)
merge_note: All three passes had this code. Pass 2's version was broader ('whether to act', including drinking after surgery); passes 1 and 3 focused on professional care, so the merged name follows them. Pass 1 also included appointment expectations, which the majority treated as General health facts.

name: Personal plan or recommendations
definition: The participant states personal wellness or fitness goals and asks for tailored recommendations, such as foods, meal ideas, supplements or a routine. The help wanted is a plan or product suggestion fitted to their goals, not treatment of a problem.
signs:
- States goals such as fat loss, muscle gain or toning
- Lists current diet, supplements, weight or budget
- "Please recommend specific foods" or "suggest ... ideas"
- Asks for a supplement, food or product to meet a wellness or fitness GOAL
closest_other: Ask what to do or whether it is safe
how_it_differs: This code is goal-driven planning for diet, supplements or routine. If the focus is easing or treating a current symptom or problem, use Ask what to do or whether it is safe. A supplement or product asked for to treat named conditions is Ask what to do or whether it is safe; code this one as well only if a wellness or fitness goal is also stated.
example_1: "I want to discover affordable, healthy foods that will help me achieve my fitness and wellness goals." (69a1ae3c)
example_2: "fat loss, muscle gain and increasing testosterone are the main objectives." (69fcf529)
merge_note: All three passes agreed on 69a1ae3c, 69fcf529 and 69f4ca1a. Pass 3 also included 66fd6acd (incorporating an article into a wellness project); passes 1 and 2 put it under Help with a text task. Name broadened from pass 1's 'diet or supplement' to cover routines.
